prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1083; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving two vehicles. The claimant reports neck pain and has retained counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the claimant's policy and confirmed the driver is named on it. Coverage was in force at the time of the loss.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report and witness statements. Both confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle when the impact occurred, and the other driver describes the accident the same way.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the repair estimate were reviewed. The damage is largely consistent with the impact described, though a few old scratches on the rear bumper may predate this loss and have been noted separately.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the initial medical records. The whiplash diagnosis fits the type and force of the collision well, and no prior injury to the neck has been identified in the records received.

Entry 6: Claimant's account has stayed consistent across every conversation, including the recorded statement and the follow-up call with counsel present. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so the medical file is being reviewed.

Entry 7: Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy's effective date. Reserve reviewed and claim remains under evaluation pending the completed treatment records.
